annotations.title: Find what elsewhere in the folder says the same

description: Find the blocks of other documents closest in meaning to one block of a page, or to a question in your own words - passages that restate a decision or cover the same ground, whether or not anything links them. Folio works this out with a small embedding model on the reader's machine, only for documents below a FOLIO.md whose related section asks for it. Take the block's id from folio_document; a short structural line or a block repeated word for word across documents answers no blocks. For links between documents use folio_query over folio.links. Answers {asked: false} where no declaration asks; else {asked: true, state: {status: installing, downloading, indexing, ready or failed, done, total, message}, related: [{path, block, lines: [first, last], title, text: the block's words, closeness: the cosine of the two vectors, higher is closer}], version}; only status ready answers blocks, so while indexing ask again shortly. A list cut to fit one answer adds omitted, the entries each list left out, and narrow, how to ask for less.

block.description: The block's id, 8 hex characters, as folio_document lists it

path.description: The page's path, relative to the served folder or absolute under it, such as notes/plan.md; omit with question

question.description: Words to find the closest blocks to instead of a block

source.description: The file the block's text comes from when an include brings it onto the page; omit for the page's own blocks

name: folio_related
